question_text: A data analyst copies a formula containing the reference A1 from cell C1 down to cell C3. What will the reference become in C3?
options: A1, because relative references do not change when copied
A3, because relative references shift rows to match the destination
$A$1, because Excel locks references when copying downward
C3, because the reference shifts to match the current column
correct_answer: A3, because relative references shift rows to match the destination

question_text: A formula uses the reference $A$1 and is copied three columns to the right and two rows down. What does the reference become in the new cell?
options: D3, because both coordinates shift with the copy direction
$A$1, because both the column and row are locked by dollar signs
$D$3, because dollar signs only affect the direction of copying
A3, because only the row coordinate remains unchanged
correct_answer: $A$1, because both the column and row are locked by dollar signs

question_text: A formula uses the mixed reference $A1 and is copied two columns to the right. What happens to the reference?
options: The reference becomes $C3, because both coordinates are free to move
The reference stays $A1, because the column is locked and cannot shift right
The reference becomes $A3, because the row shifts but the column remains fixed
The reference becomes C1, because mixed references release all locks on copy
correct_answer: The reference stays $A1, because the column is locked and cannot shift right

question_text: Which keyboard key toggles between relative, absolute, and mixed cell reference types after a cell address has been typed in a formula?
options: F2, which activates cell editing mode and cycles reference types
F4, which inserts dollar signs to cycle through the reference types
Ctrl+Shift+F, which opens the Format Cells dialog for reference settings
Alt+Enter, which locks the current cell coordinate and toggles types
correct_answer: F4, which inserts dollar signs to cycle through the reference types

question_text: An analyst wants only entries from a pre-approved list to be accepted in a column of a worksheet. Which Excel feature should be used to enforce this restriction?
options: Conditional Formatting with a highlight rule targeting invalid values
Data Validation with the List validation type applied to the target range
Find and Replace to overwrite entries that do not match the approved list
A COUNTIF formula that alerts the user when an incorrect value is entered
correct_answer: Data Validation with the List validation type applied to the target range

question_text: A manager sets up data validation on a salary column to accept only whole numbers between 1000 and 10000. A staff member enters 5000.5. What does Excel do?
options: It rounds the value to 5001 automatically to fit within the validation rule
It accepts the value because 5000.5 falls within the numeric range specified
It triggers the error alert because 5000.5 is not a whole number as required
It clears the cell and waits for the next entry without displaying a message
correct_answer: It triggers the error alert because 5000.5 is not a whole number as required

question_text: Which Data Validation tab allows a user to display a descriptive message when a validated cell is selected, before any data is entered?
options: The Error Alert tab, which shows a message after invalid data is submitted
The Settings tab, which contains the validation criteria and display options
The Input Message tab, which displays a comment when the cell is selected
The Custom tab, which accepts a formula that controls message display
correct_answer: The Input Message tab, which displays a comment when the cell is selected

question_text: A team lead applies conditional formatting to highlight all sales figures greater than 50,000 in green. A rep submits a figure of 49,999. Which outcome correctly describes this scenario?
options: The cell is highlighted green because the value is close to the threshold
The cell is not highlighted because it does not satisfy the greater-than rule
Excel prompts the user to confirm whether the rule should apply to this value
The cell is highlighted with a warning color because it narrowly misses the rule
correct_answer: The cell is not highlighted because it does not satisfy the greater-than rule

question_text: A large dataset contains multiple blank rows scattered throughout. An analyst wants to delete all blank rows simultaneously without manually hunting each one. Which technique achieves this most efficiently?
options: Sort the dataset by the first column so blank rows migrate to the bottom for deletion
Use Find and Replace to replace blank cells with a placeholder and then delete manually
Use Go To Special to select Blanks, then right-click and delete entire rows at once
Apply a filter to the first column and delete visible rows one section at a time
correct_answer: Use Go To Special to select Blanks, then right-click and delete entire rows at once

question_text: After pressing F5 and clicking 'Special...' in Excel, what is the primary purpose of selecting the 'Blanks' option?
options: To format all empty cells in the selected range with a background color simultaneously
To navigate to the first empty cell in the worksheet for faster data entry
To simultaneously select all empty cells in the chosen range for bulk operations
To count the number of blank cells and display the total in the status bar
correct_answer: To simultaneously select all empty cells in the chosen range for bulk operations

question_text: An analyst presses Ctrl + H. After typing 'Gana' in the Find box and 'Ghana' in the Replace box, they click Replace All. What is the most accurate description of this action?
options: Excel corrects only the first instance of 'Gana' found in the active cell's column
Excel replaces every instance of 'Gana' in the workbook with 'Ghana' simultaneously
Excel prompts the user to confirm each replacement individually before proceeding
Excel creates a new column with corrected values and leaves the original column intact
correct_answer: Excel replaces every instance of 'Gana' in the workbook with 'Ghana' simultaneously

question_text: A user applies a filter to a dataset and selects only the 'Accra' value from the Region column. What happens to rows that do not contain 'Accra' in the Region column?
options: They are permanently deleted from the worksheet to reduce dataset size
They are moved to a new worksheet named 'Filtered Results' automatically
They are temporarily hidden from view while the original data remains intact
They are greyed out in the worksheet but remain partially visible to the user
correct_answer: They are temporarily hidden from view while the original data remains intact

question_text: What is the keyboard shortcut that both activates and deactivates AutoFilter drop-down arrows on a selected dataset?
options: Ctrl + Shift + F, which opens the custom filter dialog for the selected range
Ctrl + Shift + L, which toggles the AutoFilter drop-down arrows on and off
Alt + D + F + F, which applies a filter and then immediately removes it
F5 then Enter, which activates filter mode and hides unmatched rows
correct_answer: Ctrl + Shift + L, which toggles the AutoFilter drop-down arrows on and off

question_text: According to the BODMAS rule applied by Excel when evaluating formulas, which operation is performed first in the expression =2+3*4^2?
options: Addition, because the plus sign appears first from left to right in the expression
Multiplication, because it ranks higher than addition in the BODMAS hierarchy
The exponent (Orders), because Orders are evaluated before Multiplication in BODMAS
Division, because it shares equal priority with multiplication and appears earlier
correct_answer: The exponent (Orders), because Orders are evaluated before Multiplication in BODMAS

question_text: A cell contains the formula =SUM(B2:B10). The range B2:B10 contains a mix of numbers and blank cells. What does the SUM function return?
options: An error, because blank cells cause SUM to fail when mixed with numeric values
The total of only the numeric values, because SUM ignores blank cells automatically
Zero for the entire range, because blank cells count as zero and skew the result
The average of the numeric values, because blank cells reduce the effective range
correct_answer: The total of only the numeric values, because SUM ignores blank cells automatically

question_text: A dataset has 20 rows. Ten rows contain numbers, five rows contain text, and five rows are blank. What value does =COUNT(A1:A20) return?
options: 20, because COUNT includes all cells in the specified range without exception
15, because COUNT includes all non-blank cells regardless of their data type
10, because COUNT only counts cells that contain numeric values
5, because COUNT only counts the rows that contain text entries
correct_answer: 10, because COUNT only counts cells that contain numeric values

question_text: In the same dataset with 20 rows (ten numbers, five text, five blank), what value does =COUNTA(A1:A20) return?
options: 20, because COUNTA counts all cells including blank ones in the range
15, because COUNTA counts every non-empty cell regardless of data type
10, because COUNTA is identical to COUNT and only counts numeric cells
5, because COUNTA specifically targets text-only cells in a range
correct_answer: 15, because COUNTA counts every non-empty cell regardless of data type

question_text: An analyst needs to calculate the average of a range but some rows in that range are hidden by a filter. Which function calculates the average of only the visible rows?
options: AVERAGE, because it automatically detects and skips hidden rows in a filtered list
AVERAGEIF, because it applies a criteria check that excludes hidden cell values
AGGREGATE, because it can perform calculations while ignoring hidden rows
SUBTOTAL, when used with function number 1, to compute a visible-only average
correct_answer: AGGREGATE, because it can perform calculations while ignoring hidden rows

question_text: A formula reads =IF(Salary>5000, "Rich", "Not Rich"). If the Salary cell contains the value 5000 exactly, what does the formula return?
options: "Rich", because 5000 is equal to the threshold and equality satisfies greater than
An error, because the IF function cannot evaluate when the value matches exactly
"Not Rich", because 5000 does not satisfy the strictly greater-than condition
A blank cell, because the condition is ambiguous when the value equals the threshold
correct_answer: "Not Rich", because 5000 does not satisfy the strictly greater-than condition

question_text: Which statement most accurately distinguishes the IFS function from a nested IF function?
options: IFS evaluates conditions one at a time and is a cleaner alternative to multiple nested IFs
IFS is limited to two conditions while nested IF can handle unlimited logical tests
IFS returns TRUE or FALSE while nested IF returns any text or number specified
IFS requires AND or OR inside it, while nested IF handles logic independently
correct_answer: IFS evaluates conditions one at a time and is a cleaner alternative to multiple nested IFs

question_text: A formula reads =AND(A1>10, B1<5). Cell A1 contains 15 and cell B1 contains 7. What does this formula return?
options: TRUE, because at least one of the two conditions is satisfied by the cell values
FALSE, because AND requires every argument to be true and B1<5 is not satisfied
TRUE, because AND returns TRUE when the majority of conditions are satisfied
15, because AND returns the value of the first condition that evaluates to true
correct_answer: FALSE, because AND requires every argument to be true and B1<5 is not satisfied

question_text: A formula reads =OR(A1>10, B1<5). Cell A1 contains 15 and cell B1 contains 7. What does this formula return?
options: FALSE, because OR requires all conditions to be true and B1<5 is not met
TRUE, because OR returns TRUE when at least one condition is satisfied
15, because OR returns the value of the first condition that evaluates to true
FALSE, because OR only returns TRUE when the last argument in the list is true
correct_answer: TRUE, because OR returns TRUE when at least one condition is satisfied

question_text: A formula reads =IFERROR(VLOOKUP(A1,B:C,2,FALSE), "Not Found"). The lookup value in A1 does not exist in column B. What does the formula return?
options: A #N/A error, because IFERROR only suppresses division-by-zero errors
"Not Found", because IFERROR intercepts the VLOOKUP error and returns the custom text
A blank cell, because IFERROR replaces all errors with an empty string by default
0, because IFERROR converts lookup errors into zero for numeric compatibility
correct_answer: "Not Found", because IFERROR intercepts the VLOOKUP error and returns the custom text

question_text: An analyst writes =SUMIF(A2:A10, "Persis Yentumi", B2:B10). What is this formula calculating?
options: The count of cells in A2:A10 that contain the name Persis Yentumi
The sum of values in B2:B10 for every row where A2:A10 equals Persis Yentumi
The average score in B2:B10 across all rows that match the name in A2:A10
The maximum value in B2:B10 corresponding to the name Persis Yentumi in column A
correct_answer: The sum of values in B2:B10 for every row where A2:A10 equals Persis Yentumi

question_text: A SUMIFS formula sums scores for female respondents older than 30. The formula has arguments: sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, criteria_range2, criteria2. What does criteria_range2 represent in this context?
options: The range containing gender values used to match the second criterion specified
The range containing age values used to evaluate whether the age exceeds 30
The column holding the scores that will be totalled when all conditions are met
A duplicate of criteria_range1 used to verify the gender criterion is consistent
correct_answer: The range containing age values used to evaluate whether the age exceeds 30

question_text: How does COUNTIFS fundamentally differ from COUNTIF in terms of criteria handling?
options: COUNTIFS counts cells containing text while COUNTIF exclusively counts numeric cells
COUNTIFS evaluates multiple criteria across multiple ranges while COUNTIF handles a single criterion
COUNTIFS sums matched cells while COUNTIF only counts them without any aggregation
COUNTIFS requires an absolute reference while COUNTIF works with any reference type
correct_answer: COUNTIFS evaluates multiple criteria across multiple ranges while COUNTIF handles a single criterion

question_text: A VLOOKUP formula is set up to find an employee's department. The fourth argument is set to FALSE. What does this argument specify?
options: That the function should return the nearest approximate match if an exact match is unavailable
That the function must find an exact match and returns an error if none is found
That the search should proceed from the last column of the table to the first column
That the lookup value column does not need to be sorted in any particular order
correct_answer: That the function must find an exact match and returns an error if none is found

question_text: A user has a table where product names are in row 1 and prices are in row 3. They want to find a price by product name. Which lookup function is best suited for this horizontal table structure?
options: VLOOKUP, because it searches vertically through the first column of any table range
HLOOKUP, because it searches across the top row and returns a value from a specified row below
XLOOKUP, because it is the only function capable of searching horizontally in Excel
INDEX, because it retrieves values by row and column intersection without needing MATCH
correct_answer: HLOOKUP, because it searches across the top row and returns a value from a specified row below

question_text: An analyst uses XLOOKUP instead of VLOOKUP. Which capability does XLOOKUP offer that VLOOKUP cannot perform?
options: XLOOKUP can return values from multiple columns in a single formula call
XLOOKUP can search in any direction, including returning values to the left of the lookup column
XLOOKUP automatically adjusts the column index when columns are inserted into a table
XLOOKUP ignores errors internally without requiring a wrapper IFERROR function
correct_answer: XLOOKUP can search in any direction, including returning values to the left of the lookup column

question_text: A formula uses =INDEX(B2:B20, MATCH("Lagos", A2:A20, 0)). What role does the MATCH function play in this combination?
options: It returns the value stored in the cell that matches Lagos within the range A2:A20
It finds the row position of Lagos in A2:A20, which INDEX then uses to retrieve the B column value
It counts the number of times Lagos appears in A2:A20 and passes the count to INDEX
It validates that Lagos exists in the range before allowing INDEX to execute the lookup
correct_answer: It finds the row position of Lagos in A2:A20, which INDEX then uses to retrieve the B column value

question_text: A user imports customer names from a web database and notices extra spaces between words like 'John   Doe'. Which function removes these extra spaces while keeping one space between each word?
options: CLEAN, which removes extra spacing along with non-printable characters from text
TRIM, which reduces multiple spaces between words to a single space and removes leading and trailing ones
PROPER, which reformats text casing and in doing so eliminates double spacing errors
SUBSTITUTE, which replaces specific space characters throughout the text string
correct_answer: TRIM, which reduces multiple spaces between words to a single space and removes leading and trailing ones

question_text: Data imported from a legacy system contains invisible non-printable characters that corrupt formula results. Which function is specifically designed to remove these characters?
options: TRIM, which strips whitespace from both ends and between words in a text string
SUBSTITUTE, which replaces specified characters with empty strings throughout the text
CLEAN, which removes non-printable characters commonly found in imported or web data
FIND, which locates the position of unwanted characters so they can be removed manually
correct_answer: CLEAN, which removes non-printable characters commonly found in imported or web data

question_text: A column contains names in all uppercase like 'WILLIAM OCLOO'. A stakeholder needs them in title case. Which function converts this to 'William Ocloo'?
options: UPPER, which forces all characters in the text string to uppercase letters
LOWER, which converts all characters to lowercase including the first letter of each word
PROPER, which capitalizes the first letter of every word and lowercases the rest
TRIM, which reformats text spacing and as a side effect normalizes the letter casing
correct_answer: PROPER, which capitalizes the first letter of every word and lowercases the rest

question_text: An analyst needs the first 4 characters of product codes stored in column A (e.g., 'PROD1234' should return 'PROD'). Which function achieves this?
options: RIGHT(A1, 4), which extracts the last 4 characters from the end of the text string
MID(A1, 1, 4), which starts at position 1 and extracts 4 characters from the middle
LEFT(A1, 4), which pulls the first 4 characters from the beginning of the text string
FIND(A1, 4), which locates character position 4 and returns the surrounding text
correct_answer: LEFT(A1, 4), which pulls the first 4 characters from the beginning of the text string

question_text: A cell contains 'EXCEL2025MASTERY'. An analyst wants to extract 'MASTERY' which starts at position 10. Which formula is correct?
options: LEFT(A1, 7), which extracts the first 7 characters starting from the left of the string
RIGHT(A1, 7), which extracts the last 7 characters from the right end of the string
MID(A1, 10, 7), which starts at position 10 and extracts the next 7 characters
FIND("MASTERY", A1), which returns the starting position of MASTERY within the string
correct_answer: MID(A1, 10, 7), which starts at position 10 and extracts the next 7 characters

question_text: A formula reads =CONCATENATE(A1, " ", B1) where A1 contains 'William' and B1 contains 'Ocloo'. What is the result?
options: WilliamOcloo, because CONCATENATE joins text without adding any characters between them
William Ocloo, because a space character has been included as the middle argument
William,Ocloo, because CONCATENATE separates text values with a comma by default
Ocloo William, because CONCATENATE reverses the order of arguments automatically
correct_answer: William Ocloo, because a space character has been included as the middle argument

question_text: The FIND function is described as case-sensitive. How does this differ from using it to locate text compared to the SEARCH function?
options: FIND returns the character count of the found text while SEARCH returns the starting position
FIND requires the text to match exactly in case, while SEARCH treats upper and lower case as equal
FIND works with numbers and text while SEARCH is limited to searching within text strings only
FIND returns a TRUE/FALSE result while SEARCH returns the numeric position of the found text
correct_answer: FIND requires the text to match exactly in case, while SEARCH treats upper and lower case as equal

question_text: A user converts a data range to a table using Ctrl + T. Which key automatic behavior makes tables especially valuable for dashboard reporting?
options: The table automatically creates a pivot table from the data range when converted
The table automatically expands its range when new rows or columns are added
The table automatically calculates and displays grand totals for all numeric columns
The table automatically applies conditional formatting based on the values inserted
correct_answer: The table automatically expands its range when new rows or columns are added

question_text: In the context of a Star Schema data model, a Fact table and a Dimension table serve distinct purposes. Which statement correctly identifies the role of the Fact table?
options: It provides descriptive context such as product names, regions, and customer segments
It stores quantitative events or transactions such as sales, revenue, and login counts
It contains unique primary keys that link to the foreign keys in Dimension tables
It holds a small number of rows that describe the 'Who, What, Where' of each event
correct_answer: It stores quantitative events or transactions such as sales, revenue, and login counts

question_text: A data model contains a Products table (ProductID, Name, Category) and a Sales table (SalesID, ProductID, Revenue). What type of relationship exists between the Products and Sales tables?
options: One-to-One, because each ProductID in Products matches exactly one ProductID in Sales
Many-to-Many, because each product can have many sales and each sale can involve many products
One-to-Many, because one product in the Products table relates to many sales records in the Sales table
Many-to-One, because the Sales table is the primary table and Products is subordinate to it
correct_answer: One-to-Many, because one product in the Products table relates to many sales records in the Sales table

question_text: A field such as 'Region' (e.g., North, South, East) would be classified in a data model as which type?
options: A Measure, because regions can be counted and aggregated mathematically
A Continuous field, because regions form an unbroken sequence of geographic values
A Dimension, because regions are qualitative categories used to slice and group data
A Fact, because regions represent recorded business events within the data model
correct_answer: A Dimension, because regions are qualitative categories used to slice and group data

question_text: In a chart, 'Revenue' (a numeric value that can be summed or averaged) would be classified as which type of data field?
options: A Dimension, because revenue is used to label and categorize different business regions
A Discrete field, because revenue is counted in individual units such as dollars or cedis
A Measure, because revenue is a quantitative value that supports mathematical operations
A Continuous header field, because revenue creates group headings along the chart axis
correct_answer: A Measure, because revenue is a quantitative value that supports mathematical operations

question_text: Which statement correctly explains the visual impact of Discrete data versus Continuous data when placed on a chart?
options: Discrete data creates a continuous axis while Continuous data creates distinct group headers
Discrete data creates headers or categories while Continuous data creates a graduated axis
Discrete and Continuous data both produce axes but differ in the direction they are plotted
Discrete data produces a bar chart while Continuous data forces Excel to produce a line chart
correct_answer: Discrete data creates headers or categories while Continuous data creates a graduated axis

question_text: An analyst needs to summarize monthly revenue by country from a 10,000-row dataset without altering the original data. Which Excel feature is purpose-built for this task?
options: A filtered table, because filtering by country groups rows and sums revenue automatically
Conditional Formatting, because it can group data by color based on country and revenue thresholds
A Pivot Table, because it summarizes and analyzes datasets without modifying the source data
The AGGREGATE function, because it computes grouped totals while ignoring hidden rows
correct_answer: A Pivot Table, because it summarizes and analyzes datasets without modifying the source data

question_text: When building a Pivot Table, an analyst drags the 'Country' field to the Rows area and the 'Monthly Revenue' field to the Values area. What conceptual rule does this follow?
options: Placing a Continuous field in Rows and a Discrete field in Values for accurate grouping
Placing a Dimension field in Rows and a Measure field in Values to summarize by category
Placing a Measure in Rows and a Dimension in Values to compute revenue per country
Placing a Fact field in Rows and a Dimension field in Values to connect the data tables
correct_answer: Placing a Dimension field in Rows and a Measure field in Values to summarize by category

question_text: An analyst copies and pastes an existing Pivot Table within the same worksheet. What is the primary reason this technique is useful?
options: It creates a backup copy of the Pivot Table in case the original is accidentally modified
It allows a second summary view to be built quickly by replacing fields without recreating from scratch
It doubles the dataset connection so two Pivot Tables can query different data sources simultaneously
It automatically links the two Pivot Tables so changes to one are reflected in the other
correct_answer: It allows a second summary view to be built quickly by replacing fields without recreating from scratch

question_text: A slicer is inserted from Pivot Table A and is used to filter the report. By default, which tables does this slicer filter?
options: All Pivot Tables in the entire workbook regardless of their data source
Only the Pivot Table from which the slicer was originally inserted
All Pivot Tables located on the same worksheet as the slicer
All Pivot Tables that are connected to the same named Excel Table source
correct_answer: Only the Pivot Table from which the slicer was originally inserted

question_text: A report contains three Pivot Tables and one slicer. An analyst wants the slicer to filter all three tables simultaneously. What is the correct procedure?
options: Insert three separate slicers, one for each Pivot Table, then link them using slicer settings
Right-click the slicer, choose Report Connections, and check the boxes for all three Pivot Tables
Move all three Pivot Tables to the same worksheet so the slicer applies automatically
Copy the slicer and paste it next to each Pivot Table so each has its own dedicated filter
correct_answer: Right-click the slicer, choose Report Connections, and check the boxes for all three Pivot Tables

question_text: A dataset has a Revenue column and a Cost column. An analyst wants a Profit column in the Pivot Table without adding a new column to the raw dataset. Which Pivot Table feature achieves this?
options: A Slicer, which filters the Pivot Table to show only profitable rows by category
A Calculated Field, which applies a formula to existing fields to derive a new Pivot Table field
Report Connections, which link multiple Pivot Tables to share computed column values
A Pivot Chart, which automatically generates a derived profit line from revenue and cost fields
correct_answer: A Calculated Field, which applies a formula to existing fields to derive a new Pivot Table field

question_text: Power Query is described as an ETL tool. In the context of data preparation in Excel, what do the letters E, T, and L stand for?
options: Edit, Transfer, and Link, describing how Power Query moves data between workbooks
Export, Template, and Load, describing how Power Query formats data for reporting
Extract, Transform, and Load, describing the steps of connecting, cleaning, and applying data
Evaluate, Test, and Label, describing how Power Query validates and categorizes data fields
correct_answer: Extract, Transform, and Load, describing the steps of connecting, cleaning, and applying data

question_text: A key feature of Power Query is the Applied Steps pane. What happens when a user clicks 'Refresh' on a Power Query connection after receiving next month's updated data file?
options: Power Query opens the data source file so the user can manually reapply each transformation step
Power Query re-runs all previously recorded transformation steps automatically on the new data
Power Query deletes the old Applied Steps and asks the user to re-enter the transformation logic
Power Query creates a new query sheet and applies the steps only to the newly added rows
correct_answer: Power Query re-runs all previously recorded transformation steps automatically on the new data

question_text: A raw CSV file has column headers in the first data row rather than as actual column headers. Which Power Query action resolves this to make the data model-ready?
options: Remove Top Rows, which deletes the header row so that the data starts cleanly from row two
Split Column, which separates the header row content into distinct individual column names
Use First Row as Headers, which promotes the first row of data to become the column names
Change Data Type, which reassigns the header row values to the correct column categories
correct_answer: Use First Row as Headers, which promotes the first row of data to become the column names

question_text: In Power Query, why is setting the correct Data Type for each column a critical step before loading data into Excel?
options: It determines the sort order of the column values when data is loaded into the workbook
It controls the visual formatting of the cells, such as whether numbers appear as currency
It ensures Excel interprets values correctly, so dates are recognized as dates and numbers as decimals
It restricts data entry in the loaded worksheet to only values matching the assigned type
correct_answer: It ensures Excel interprets values correctly, so dates are recognized as dates and numbers as decimals

question_text: Power Pivot is described as allowing Excel to go beyond its standard row limits. Why is this capability critical for enterprise-level data analysis?
options: Because Excel's standard grid is limited to 1,048,576 rows, and Power Pivot processes millions of rows in its in-memory engine
Because Power Pivot compresses each row to a smaller size, allowing more rows to fit within the same grid limit
Because Power Pivot splits the data across multiple worksheets automatically to bypass the row limit
Because Power Pivot connects to external databases and only downloads a summary rather than all rows
correct_answer: Because Excel's standard grid is limited to 1,048,576 rows, and Power Pivot processes millions of rows in its in-memory engine

question_text: In Power Pivot's Diagram View, two tables are displayed with a line between them showing '1' on one end and '*' on the other. What does this diagram communicate?
options: A Many-to-Many relationship where both tables contain repeating values for the linked field
A One-to-One relationship where each record in both tables matches exactly one record
A One-to-Many relationship where one unique record in the first table relates to many records in the second
An error in the relationship configuration that must be resolved before the Pivot Table can function
correct_answer: A One-to-Many relationship where one unique record in the first table relates to many records in the second

question_text: A Many-to-Many relationship in a Power Pivot data model is flagged as potentially problematic. What specific analytical issue can arise from an unmanaged Many-to-Many relationship?
options: The data model fails to load any data into Pivot Tables, making the relationship non-functional
Filter directions become one-directional only, preventing slicers from working on either table
Values can be double-counted in reports because each row in one table may match multiple rows in the other
The relationship causes all measures to calculate incorrectly by summing only unique row combinations
correct_answer: Values can be double-counted in reports because each row in one table may match multiple rows in the other

question_text: In a Power Pivot model with a Single Direction filter, the filter flows from the Dimension table to the Fact table. What does this mean practically when a user selects a product in a slicer?
options: The product selection filters the sales list to show only records for that product, but the product list is unaffected by clicking a sale
The product selection filters both the sales list and the product list simultaneously in both directions
The product selection filters the product list downward but has no effect on the related sales records
The product slicer becomes disabled because Single Direction filters only work on Fact-to-Dimension flows
correct_answer: The product selection filters the sales list to show only records for that product, but the product list is unaffected by clicking a sale

question_text: Goal Seek is used when a user knows the desired output but not the required input. In which scenario is Goal Seek the most appropriate tool?
options: A manager wants to compare three pricing strategies and see the profit for each scenario
An analyst wants to predict future sales for the next 12 months based on historical trends
A business owner needs to know how many units must be sold to achieve a profit of GHS 1,000,000
A finance team wants to calculate the average revenue across five different regional branches
correct_answer: A business owner needs to know how many units must be sold to achieve a profit of GHS 1,000,000

question_text: When using Goal Seek, the 'By Changing Cell' field must reference which type of cell?
options: A cell containing a formula that calculates the desired target output value
A cell containing a static input value that the formula depends on as a variable
Any empty cell that Excel can use as temporary storage during the iteration process
A cell containing the current result to confirm Goal Seek targets the right calculation
correct_answer: A cell containing a static input value that the formula depends on as a variable

question_text: A CFO wants to model three versions of next year's budget: Optimistic, Base Case, and Pessimistic, each with different revenue and cost assumptions. Which Excel tool is best suited for storing and switching between these versions?
options: Goal Seek, which adjusts a single variable to match a target result for each scenario
Forecast Sheet, which uses historical data to project values for future planning periods
Scenario Manager, which stores multiple sets of input values that can be displayed or compared
Conditional Formatting, which highlights cells that match the optimistic or pessimistic thresholds
correct_answer: Scenario Manager, which stores multiple sets of input values that can be displayed or compared

question_text: A Scenario Summary report is generated after setting up Best Case and Worst Case scenarios. What information does this report contain?
options: A chart comparing the Best Case and Worst Case scenarios as line graphs over time
A table listing the changing cell values and result cell values for each named scenario
A pivot table grouping scenarios by the magnitude of difference in the result cells
A conditional formatting map that colour-codes which scenario performs best per variable
correct_answer: A table listing the changing cell values and result cell values for each named scenario

question_text: A Forecast Sheet requires two specific columns of data to generate predictions. What are these two required columns?
options: A column of numeric identifiers and a column of product category labels for the timeline
A column of dates forming a timeline and a column of corresponding values such as sales figures
A column of target values and a column of actual values for comparison-based forecasting
A column of dimensions and a column of measures drawn from a connected Pivot Table
correct_answer: A column of dates forming a timeline and a column of corresponding values such as sales figures

question_text: When Excel generates a Forecast Sheet, it includes 'Confidence Intervals' in the output chart. What do these intervals represent?
options: The range of historical data values used as input for the forecasting algorithm
The upper and lower bounds within which future values are statistically likely to fall
The margin of error in the historical data that was detected and corrected by Excel
The percentage confidence that the user's selected date range is appropriate for the forecast
correct_answer: The upper and lower bounds within which future values are statistically likely to fall

question_text: A user types =MAX(A1:A10) and =MIN(A1:A10) for a range containing [3, 7, 15, 2, 9]. What are the two values returned by these functions respectively?
options: MAX returns 9 and MIN returns 3, because 9 is the most recent entry and 3 appeared first
MAX returns 15 and MIN returns 2, because MAX finds the largest and MIN finds the smallest value
MAX returns 7.2 and MIN returns 2, because MAX calculates the average and MIN finds the smallest
MAX returns 15 and MIN returns 3, because MAX is the highest and MIN skips the lowest outlier
correct_answer: MAX returns 15 and MIN returns 2, because MAX finds the largest and MIN finds the smallest value

question_text: The AVERAGE function is applied to a range where one cell contains the text 'N/A' and five cells contain numbers. What does AVERAGE return?
options: An error, because the presence of any text in the range makes AVERAGE unable to calculate
Zero, because AVERAGE treats text values as zero and includes them in the denominator
The mean of the five numeric values only, because AVERAGE ignores text cells automatically
The sum of the five numbers divided by six, because AVERAGE counts text cells in the divisor
correct_answer: The mean of the five numeric values only, because AVERAGE ignores text cells automatically

question_text: What is the functional difference between the Name Box and the Formula Bar in the Excel interface?
options: The Name Box displays and edits cell content while the Formula Bar shows only the cell address
The Name Box displays the cell address and navigates to cells, while the Formula Bar shows and edits cell content
The Name Box executes formulas while the Formula Bar is used only for static text entry
The Name Box formats cell references while the Formula Bar previews how formulas will be printed
correct_answer: The Name Box displays the cell address and navigates to cells, while the Formula Bar shows and edits cell content

question_text: The Auto-Fill Handle in Excel is described as the small green square in the bottom-right corner of an active cell. Besides copying data, what additional capability does it provide?
options: It formats the destination cells to match the source cell's colour scheme automatically
It inserts blank rows between each copied value to create visual separation in the data
It completes a series such as dates or sequential numbers by clicking and dragging
It validates the copied values against a data validation list applied to the destination range
correct_answer: It completes a series such as dates or sequential numbers by clicking and dragging

question_text: A workbook contains five worksheets. The Worksheet Tabs are visible at the bottom of the screen. What is their primary function?
options: To display the active cell reference and allow navigation to any named range in the workbook
To show formula audit trails between worksheets when tracing precedents across sheets
To allow the user to select and navigate between individual worksheets within the workbook
To filter the data visible in the current worksheet based on the worksheet tab selected
correct_answer: To allow the user to select and navigate between individual worksheets within the workbook

question_text: The Ribbon is organized into Ribbon Tabs, the Ribbon itself, and Ribbon Groups. How do these three elements relate hierarchically?
options: Ribbon Groups contain Ribbon Tabs, which together form the Ribbon displayed across the top
Ribbon Tabs organize commands by topic, the Ribbon displays the commands beneath the tabs, and Ribbon Groups cluster related commands together
The Ribbon contains the Ribbon Tabs which are subdivided by Ribbon Groups into individual commands
Ribbon Tabs display individual commands while Ribbon Groups organize the tabs into broader categories
correct_answer: Ribbon Tabs organize commands by topic, the Ribbon displays the commands beneath the tabs, and Ribbon Groups cluster related commands together

question_text: A user clicks the Dialog Box Launcher in the Font group of the Home Tab. What does this action do?
options: It opens a floating toolbar with quick access to the most recently used Font commands
It expands the Ribbon group to display all available commands that were previously hidden
It opens a full dialog box containing advanced Font formatting options beyond what is on the Ribbon
It saves the current font settings as a default style applied to all future new workbooks
correct_answer: It opens a full dialog box containing advanced Font formatting options beyond what is on the Ribbon

question_text: An Excel workbook has 10 worksheets but the analyst only needs to work on 3 of them. The relationship between workbook and worksheets is best described as which of the following?
options: A workbook is a single page of data while worksheets are separate files linked within a folder
A workbook is a file containing one or more worksheets, similar to a folder holding separate pages
A workbook is a row of data entries while worksheets represent the columns that hold that data
A workbook and a worksheet refer to the same object, with the difference being the view mode only
correct_answer: A workbook is a file containing one or more worksheets, similar to a folder holding separate pages

question_text: A cell is described as being formed by the intersection of a row and a column. If a user clicks the cell at the intersection of column D and row 7, what is the cell's address?
options: 7D, because row numbers are stated before column letters in Excel's cell addressing system
D7, because Excel addresses cells by stating the column letter followed by the row number
Row7Col4, because Excel uses descriptive naming when referencing columns by position
4,7, because Excel uses numeric coordinates for both the column and the row reference
correct_answer: D7, because Excel addresses cells by stating the column letter followed by the row number

question_text: Which of the following is the correct notation for the 'Not equal to' relational operator in Excel formulas?
options: !=, which uses an exclamation mark followed by an equals sign as in many programming languages
≠, which is the mathematical symbol for inequality used in standard algebraic notation
<>, which uses a less-than sign followed by a greater-than sign to denote not equal
NOT=, which uses a text prefix before the equals sign to negate the comparison
correct_answer: <>, which uses a less-than sign followed by a greater-than sign to denote not equal

question_text: A VLOOKUP formula searches for a value in a table. The formula's third argument is set to 3. What does this argument specify?
options: That the search should start from the third column of the selected table range
That the result returned should come from the third column of the specified table range
That the formula should find the third occurrence of the lookup value in the table
That the lookup value should be matched against the third row at the top of the table
correct_answer: That the result returned should come from the third column of the specified table range

question_text: VLOOKUP can only look up values in the leftmost column of a table range. An analyst needs to look up a value that is to the right of the return column. Which function resolves this limitation?
options: HLOOKUP, because it searches horizontally and can return values to the left of the search row
COUNTIF, because it can reference any column in a range regardless of its position in the table
INDEX-MATCH, because MATCH finds the position and INDEX retrieves the value from any column
SUMIF, because it searches by criteria in any column and returns the sum from any other column
correct_answer: INDEX-MATCH, because MATCH finds the position and INDEX retrieves the value from any column

question_text: An analyst wants to use TRANSPOSE to reorganize a vertical list of 5 items into a horizontal row. Which method is described in the slides for using TRANSPOSE?
options: Typing =TRANSPOSE(range) and pressing Enter to flip the range from vertical to horizontal layout
Selecting a horizontal range and using Paste Special with Transpose checked after copying
Dragging the column range header to a row position while holding the Alt key for transposition
Using the Power Query Transform tab's Transpose button to flip the table orientation
correct_answer: Typing =TRANSPOSE(range) and pressing Enter to flip the range from vertical to horizontal layout

question_text: In Power Query, what is the purpose of the 'Remove Rows' feature on the Home tab?
options: It permanently deletes selected rows from the original source data file on disk
It hides specific rows from view in Power Query without affecting the data transformation steps
It removes top headers, empty bottom rows, or duplicate rows during the transformation process
It filters rows in the loaded Excel worksheet based on criteria defined in the Power Query editor
correct_answer: It removes top headers, empty bottom rows, or duplicate rows during the transformation process

question_text: A Power Query step splits a column containing 'First Name Last Name' into two separate columns. What Power Query action achieves this?
options: Promote Headers, which reassigns the first row values to create two named column headers
Split Column, which separates a single column into multiple columns using a delimiter
Change Data Type, which restructures combined text fields into typed separate columns
Remove Columns, which deletes the original column and replaces it with the split values
correct_answer: Split Column, which separates a single column into multiple columns using a delimiter

question_text: An analyst applies Conditional Formatting using a 'Greater Than' rule on a column of exam scores with a threshold of 75. A score of 75 is in the range. Is the cell highlighted?
options: Yes, because equal to the threshold satisfies the greater-than-or-equal-to condition by default
No, because the Greater Than rule is strictly greater than 75 and 75 does not exceed itself
Yes, because Conditional Formatting rounds borderline values up to apply the formatting rule
No, because Conditional Formatting only highlights values that are at least 10% above the threshold
correct_answer: No, because the Greater Than rule is strictly greater than 75 and 75 does not exceed itself

question_text: After filling blank cells using Ctrl + Enter following a Go To Special > Blanks selection, what does the Ctrl + Enter keystroke specifically do?
options: It moves the cursor to the next blank cell in the range without filling the current selection
It confirms the formula entered and fills all simultaneously selected blank cells with the typed value
It copies the value from the cell above each blank cell using a relative reference automatically
It saves the workbook and applies the typed value to only the first selected blank cell
correct_answer: It confirms the formula entered and fills all simultaneously selected blank cells with the typed value

question_text: An analyst uses Find and Replace with the 'Match Case' option enabled. The Find box contains 'ghana'. A cell contains 'Ghana'. Is this cell replaced?
options: Yes, because Find and Replace treats all text as case-insensitive regardless of the Match Case option
No, because Match Case requires the search text to match the exact capitalization in the cell
Yes, because the Match Case option only applies to replacements, not to the search step
No, because Find and Replace with Match Case only works on numeric values in the dataset
correct_answer: No, because Match Case requires the search text to match the exact capitalization in the cell

question_text: Which Excel function would an analyst use if they need to count the number of sales transactions where the Region is 'North' AND the Product Category is 'Electronics'?
options: COUNTIF, because it counts cells in a range that match a single specified criterion
SUMIFS, because it adds values that meet multiple criteria across different column ranges
COUNTIFS, because it counts cells that satisfy multiple criteria across separate ranges simultaneously
COUNT, because it counts all numeric entries in a range that the filter has already restricted
correct_answer: COUNTIFS, because it counts cells that satisfy multiple criteria across separate ranges simultaneously

question_text: A Dimension table is described as having a 'Primary Key'. What is the defining characteristic of a Primary Key in this context?
options: It is a numeric column that stores the sum of all measures associated with each dimension record
It is a column containing a unique identifier for each record that links to a Foreign Key in the Fact table
It is an automatically generated column that Power Pivot creates when a relationship is defined
It is a column that stores descriptive attributes like names and categories for each fact record
correct_answer: It is a column containing a unique identifier for each record that links to a Foreign Key in the Fact table

question_text: The slides note that in professional data modeling, One-to-One relationships are rare. What is the primary reason these relationships are typically avoided in favor of a single merged table?
options: One-to-One relationships always produce incorrect results in DAX calculations within Power Pivot
Since both tables have unique matching records, merging them into one table using Power Query is simpler and more efficient
One-to-One relationships require Bi-directional filters which severely degrade dashboard performance
Power Pivot cannot establish One-to-One relationships and displays an error when they are attempted
correct_answer: Since both tables have unique matching records, merging them into one table using Power Query is simpler and more efficient

question_text: DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) in Power Pivot is used to create custom Measures. What distinguishes a DAX Measure from a regular Calculated Field added to a raw dataset?
options: A DAX Measure modifies the underlying data in the Power Pivot table while a Calculated Field only changes the display
A DAX Measure is evaluated dynamically based on the current filter context of the Pivot Table while a raw Calculated Field is static
A DAX Measure is limited to basic arithmetic while a Calculated Field supports advanced logical operations
A DAX Measure requires the data to be sorted before it can produce accurate aggregation results
correct_answer: A DAX Measure is evaluated dynamically based on the current filter context of the Pivot Table while a raw Calculated Field is static

question_text: A user attempts to open the Power Query Editor by going to the Data Tab. What is the correct path to access Power Query from a fresh data source?
options: Data Tab > What-If Analysis > Power Query Editor
Data Tab > Get Data, then select the data source and click Transform
Insert Tab > Data Model > Open Power Query Editor
Data Tab > Data Validation > External Sources > Power Query
correct_answer: Data Tab > Get Data, then select the data source and click Transform

question_text: To enable the Power Pivot tab in Excel, a user must perform a specific activation process. What is the general category of steps required to enable it?
options: Downloading and installing a separate Power Pivot application from the Microsoft Store
Enabling Power Pivot through Excel's Add-Ins or Options settings, as it is not visible by default
Activating Power Pivot by purchasing an upgraded Microsoft 365 subscription tier
Connecting to an online Power BI workspace which automatically activates the Power Pivot tab
correct_answer: Enabling Power Pivot through Excel's Add-Ins or Options settings, as it is not visible by default

question_text: When creating a Pivot Chart directly from a Pivot Table, which tab in Excel provides the option to insert the chart?
options: The Insert Tab, which contains the Charts group for inserting standalone charts from any range
The View Tab, which allows switching between different visual representations of the Pivot Table
The PivotTable Analyze Tab, which contains the Tools group with the Pivot Chart button
The Home Tab, which includes a quick chart insertion button in the Styles group
correct_answer: The PivotTable Analyze Tab, which contains the Tools group with the Pivot Chart button

question_text: A user has a formula =B2-C2 (Revenue minus Cost) in a Pivot Table Calculated Field and names it 'Profit'. After clicking OK, where does this new 'Profit' field appear?
options: It is added as a new column in the raw dataset in the Excel worksheet source table
It appears in the PivotTable Field List and can be dragged into the Values area like any other field
It is stored in the Power Pivot data model and only accessible through DAX expressions
It creates a new worksheet with a column of profit values corresponding to each table row
correct_answer: It appears in the PivotTable Field List and can be dragged into the Values area like any other field

question_text: The AGGREGATE function is given function_number 1, option 5, and a data range. What calculation does this perform?
options: It calculates a SUM of the range while ignoring hidden rows in a filtered dataset
It calculates an AVERAGE of the range while ignoring hidden rows in a filtered dataset
It returns the COUNT of values in the range while excluding subtotals and error values
It returns the MIN value in the range while ignoring both errors and hidden row values
correct_answer: It calculates an AVERAGE of the range while ignoring hidden rows in a filtered dataset

question_text: An analyst needs to check if either the Sales column value is above 10000 OR the Units column value is above 500 to flag a record as 'High Performance'. Which formula structure achieves this correctly?
options: =IF(AND(Sales>10000, Units>500), "High Performance", "Standard")
=AND(IF(Sales>10000, "High Performance"), IF(Units>500, "High Performance"))
=IF(OR(Sales>10000, Units>500), "High Performance", "Standard")
=OR(IF(Sales>10000, "High Performance", "Standard"), IF(Units>500, "High Performance", "Standard"))
correct_answer: =IF(OR(Sales>10000, Units>500), "High Performance", "Standard")

question_text: A SUMIFS formula must sum revenue where the Region is 'North' AND the Year is 2024. Which argument order correctly reflects the SUMIFS syntax?
options: =SUMIFS(criteria1, criteria_range1, criteria2, criteria_range2, sum_range)
=SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, criteria_range2, criteria2)
=SUMIFS(criteria_range1, sum_range, criteria1, criteria_range2, criteria2)
=SUMIFS(criteria1, sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria2, criteria_range2)
correct_answer: =SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, criteria_range2, criteria2)

question_text: The Forecast Sheet tool generates a chart with Confidence Intervals shown as shaded bands. As the forecast extends further into the future, what typically happens to the width of these confidence bands?
options: The bands narrow because more data points reduce the uncertainty of the forecast model
The bands remain constant width because the model uses a fixed confidence percentage
The bands widen because uncertainty increases as predictions extend further from the historical data
The bands disappear entirely for future periods because Excel cannot calculate confidence beyond the data range
correct_answer: The bands widen because uncertainty increases as predictions extend further from the historical data

question_text: A RIGHT function is used as =RIGHT(A1, 4) on the text 'EXCEL2025'. What result does this formula produce?
options: EXCE, which is the first 4 characters extracted from the left of the text string
2025, which is the last 4 characters extracted from the right end of the text string
CEL2, which represents the middle 4 characters beginning from position 3
XCE2, which is returned because RIGHT skips the first character before extracting
correct_answer: 2025, which is the last 4 characters extracted from the right end of the text string

question_text: A user's Pivot Table filters data by the 'Year' slicer. After right-clicking the slicer and opening 'Report Connections', they check two additional Pivot Tables. What is the effect?
options: The slicer is duplicated and placed next to each of the two additional Pivot Tables automatically
The slicer now controls filtering for all three connected Pivot Tables simultaneously with a single click
The two additional Pivot Tables receive their own independent slicers linked to the Year field
The original Pivot Table loses its slicer connection and the two new tables gain filtering instead
correct_answer: The slicer now controls filtering for all three connected Pivot Tables simultaneously with a single click

question_text: The Quick Access Toolbar is described as providing 'one-click access to any frequently used command'. How does this differ functionally from the standard Ribbon?
options: The Quick Access Toolbar runs macros while the Ribbon only accesses built-in Excel features
The Quick Access Toolbar is customizable with frequently used commands while the Ribbon organizes all commands by tab and group
The Quick Access Toolbar appears only when a cell is selected while the Ribbon is always visible
The Quick Access Toolbar applies commands to the entire workbook while the Ribbon applies only to the active sheet
correct_answer: The Quick Access Toolbar is customizable with frequently used commands while the Ribbon organizes all commands by tab and group

question_text: A user is in Normal view and wants to see exactly how their spreadsheet will look when printed, with page margins visible. Which View Button should be selected?
options: Normal View, because it shows the complete working grid including all print margins
Page Break Preview, because it shows exactly where each printed page begins and ends
Page Layout View, because it shows the spreadsheet as it will appear on a printed page with margins
Full Screen View, because it removes toolbars to show the maximum area of the worksheet
correct_answer: Page Layout View, because it shows the spreadsheet as it will appear on a printed page with margins

question_text: An analyst needs to verify that a formula is referencing the correct cell. They click the cell and look at the Formula Bar. What does the Formula Bar display for a cell containing =SUM(A1:A5)?
options: The numeric result of the formula, such as 150, because the Formula Bar shows computed output
The formula text =SUM(A1:A5) itself, because the Formula Bar displays the underlying formula
The cell address of the active cell, because the Formula Bar tracks the current cell location
A highlighted range A1:A5, because the Formula Bar visually maps the formula's dependencies
correct_answer: The formula text =SUM(A1:A5) itself, because the Formula Bar displays the underlying formula

question_text: A Bi-directional cross-filter relationship is described as powerful but recommended to be used sparingly. What risk justifies this caution, particularly in Power BI Service?
options: Bi-directional filters prevent slicers from functioning correctly on either of the connected tables
Bi-directional filters can slow down dashboard performance because filters propagate in both directions simultaneously
Bi-directional filters break the Star Schema by converting One-to-Many relationships to Many-to-Many
Bi-directional filters require DAX measures to be rewritten as calculated columns to function correctly
correct_answer: Bi-directional filters can slow down dashboard performance because filters propagate in both directions simultaneously

question_text: An analyst must present a complete comparison of three pricing strategies showing the input variables and resulting profits side by side in a structured table. Which sequence of steps in Excel produces this output using the Scenario Manager?
options: Open Goal Seek, enter each strategy as a separate target value, and click Summary to compare outputs
Create a Forecast Sheet with three date columns representing each pricing strategy and click Create
Add each scenario with its changing cell values in Scenario Manager, then click Summary to generate the comparison report
Insert three Pivot Tables, one per strategy, then use a slicer to toggle between each pricing scenario
correct_answer: Add each scenario with its changing cell values in Scenario Manager, then click Summary to generate the comparison report
